title: Qubits: Computing With Superposition
summary: A qubit is a two-level quantum system: unlike a bit, it can be in superposition of 0 and 1.
body:

title: Shor's Algorithm
summary: Peter Shor (1994): a quantum algorithm factoring integers exponentially faster than known classical methods — breaking RSA if large quantum computers arrive.
body:
Peter Shor (1994): a quantum algorithm factoring integers exponentially faster than known classical methods — breaking RSA if large quantum computers arrive. The result launched quantum computing as a field.

title: Error Correction: The Real Race

title: RSA vs. Shor Demo
summary: Tiny RSA encrypt/decrypt alongside the reminder: Shor's algorithm factors the modulus that RSA's security rests on.
body:
Tiny RSA encrypt/decrypt alongside the reminder: Shor's algorithm factors the modulus that RSA's security rests on. Toy numbers, real principle.

program.code:
# Toy RSA (educational only - tiny primes!)
import math
p, q = 61, 53
n, phi = p*q, (p-1)*(q-1)
e = 17
d = pow(e, -1, phi)
msg = 42
ct = pow(msg, e, n)
pt = pow(ct, d, n)
print(f"n={n} e={e} d={d}")
print(f"{msg} -> encrypt -> {ct} -> decrypt -> {pt}")
print("Shor's algorithm factors n efficiently on a quantum computer.")
